full_judgment:
8. The only substantive argument put forward by Mr. Hassan Ariff was that the change in the mode of assessment of depreciation from the date of manufacture of the vehicle to the date of first registration of the vehicle is ultra vires the Imports and Exports (Control) Act. 1950 (hereafter referred to as the Act, 1950). 

 11. We do not find any conflict between the provision in the Act, 1950 which relates to the age of the vehicle on the date of shipping and the SRO which relate to calculation of depreciation for the purpose of computing customs duty. The purpose of determining quantum of depreciation is to give a benefit to the consumer whereby he will be burdened with a reduced or higher customs duty, which will be reflected in the price of the vehicle, depending on the length of use of the vehicle after its registration. It is undeniable that a vehicle which is registered and used for the first time sometime after its date of manufacture will be more attractive to the purchaser as having been less used, in contrast to the vehicle which is registered soon after its manufacture and is therefore used for a longer period.
